profiles: The pinned native releases and projection profiles. MySQL uses native unnamed question marks and the signed integer cast. PostgreSQL uses native numbered positions and the pg_catalog.int4 input role.
scope: An explicitly cast parameter in a result position. The value is supplied when executing a prepared statement. Native MySQL positions are local to the projection and assigned in output order. PostgreSQL positions are absolute and can repeat or be out of lexical order.
open: Parameters without a fixed target role, other cast types, parameters inside other scalar expressions, predicates, mutation operands and row bounds

Parameter.role: One bound integer projection operand with a checked native position
invariants: The containing projection closes MySQL lexical order or PostgreSQL numbered slot coverage
Parameter.meaning: Use the supplied parameter value in the fixed native cast. A NULL input produces SQL NULL. Selection, repetition and names of projected values are observable.
Parameter.sql: Emit CAST(? AS SIGNED) for MySQL or CAST($n AS pg_catalog.int4) for PostgreSQL. Preserve occurrence order and the numbered references.

ParameterProjection.role: The existing checked result and relation scope with projected parameter positions
invariants: MySQL uses exactly the ascending positions 1 through the number of occurrences
PostgreSQL references each used index from 1 through the greatest referenced index

analysis: Recognize the explicit builtin cast of a native marker, resolve its output name in the original projection, and call the same constructor and scope checks as direct construction.
observations: Ordinal output names and native integer types
Checked bind-slot correspondence with intentionally different values

finite.completeness: Observe all one- and two-position binding products. PostgreSQL additionally enumerates the unpermuted, reversed and repeated legal layouts.

faults: Replace one projected parameter value by zero while still consuming its marker
Swap visibly different parameter bindings or their output positions
trust: Pinned native parser and bind protocols
Independent vector lookup and typed output comparisons

mysql.sql: SELECT CAST(? AS DECIMAL(6,2)) AS a0
mysql.message: A projection cast requires a checked scalar integer target.

postgres.sql: SELECT CAST($1 AS pg_catalog.bytea) AS a0
postgres.message: The cast target must be pg_catalog.int4, pg_catalog.int8, pg_catalog.bool or pg_catalog.text.

observationRevision: Keep the unqualified text target as an unresolved-context negative. Observe the qualified text positive in postgres-text-conversion-v1.json. The registered unsupported-target test now names bytea and preserves the exact rejection class and schedule. Preserve the former MySQL unsigned marker input as a positive in mysql-unsigned-parameter-v1.json. Keep the signed schedule and require the integer-role refusal for a decimal cast.

unresolvedPostgreSqlCast.sql: SELECT CAST($1 AS text) AS a0
unresolvedPostgreSqlCast.message: The cast must resolve to a scalar pg_catalog target.

additionalPostgreSqlNegatives: A named target that a temporary relation may shadow in the open analysis context

resolvedCounterexample.sql: SELECT CAST(? AS UNSIGNED) AS a0
resolvedCounterexample.message: A projection cast must have the scalar MySQL SIGNED target.
